grub-v18-note: 🚀 New in V18: The script now features Headless Automation via CLI Flags! Pass -env l -auto to bypass all confirmation prompts and let the script fix GRUB silently in seconds based on auto-detection.
grub-flags-desc: V18 introduces Command-Line Arguments to bypass prompts and enable headless automation:
grub-flag-1: -env l or -env live: Force the script to assume a Live Environment (USB/ISO).
grub-flag-2: -env h or -env host: Force the script to assume a Real Machine / Host environment.
grub-flag-3: -auto: The "Ultimate Mode" flag. Bypasses all confirmation prompts (y/n), automatically assumes default mount points, and executes the repair instantly.
grub-flag-4: --version or -v: Print the current version and exit.
grub-evo-1: In-Situ (Local) Mode Detection (V16): Intelligently detects if run from the installed OS, bypassing the chroot environment to repair GRUB locally in seconds.
grub-evo-2: Dynamic UEFI 32-bit Detection (V15): Detects rare 32-bit UEFI architectures and automatically switches the GRUB target to i386-efi.
grub-evo-3: Dynamic Execution Timer (V14): Delivers gamer-style human status messages based on repair speed.
grub-evo-4: OS Prober Integration (V13): Automatically enables GRUB_DISABLE_OS_PROBER=false to ensure Windows/other distros are detected.
grub-evo-5: Legacy BIOS & Smart Target Disk Extraction (V12): Full support for i386-pc with intelligent parent disk extraction.
grub-core-1: Zero-Interaction FSTAB Parsing: Resolves UUID and PARTUUID tags instantly, mapping Btrfs subvolumes without manual input.
grub-core-2: 3-Tier Fallback System: Gracefully falls back from Pro Mode (FSTAB) to Smart Auto-Detection, and finally to Manual Input.
grub-core-3: Bulletproof Btrfs Loop: Interactive validation for complex subvolume hierarchies (@, @home, @log).
grub-core-4: VM & NVRAM Rescue: Forced --removable flag usage for stubborn UEFI firmware and QEMU/KVM environments.

grub-page-desc: Automated, secure Universal (UEFI & Legacy BIOS) bootloader rescue suite with Security Hardening, Secure Boot MOK Enrollment, LUKS Encryption Support, Chroot Health Checks, RedHat/Fedora support, and Deep Scan Intelligence.
grub-about-desc: GRUB Fixer (V23 - The "Security Hardening" Update) takes system recovery to the absolute limit. It is an automated, bulletproof Bash script designed to repair the GRUB bootloader on both UEFI and Legacy BIOS systems. V23 elevates the script into a highly-secure recovery tool by introducing dynamic MOK OTP generation, hidden LUKS password inputs, and failsafe configuration backups. This builds upon the Secure Boot Support (V22), LUKS Encryption (V21), Chroot Health Checks (V20), and Universal RedHat/Fedora Support (V19) of previous versions.
grub-v23-note: 🔒 New in V23: The script now features Advanced Security Hardening! It dynamically generates Secure Boot MOK OTPs using openssl, completely hides LUKS password inputs to prevent shoulder surfing, and automatically backs up /etc/default/grub before modifying the host system.
grub-sec-1: Anti-Shoulder Surfing: LUKS password input is now completely hidden (read -s) during the early decryption phase to protect your credentials.
grub-sec-2: Dynamic MOK OTP Generation: Replaced the hardcoded Secure Boot password with a dynamically generated, 12-character random One-Time Password.
grub-sec-3: Failsafe Config Backups: Automatically creates a timestamped backup of /etc/default/grub before making any modifications to the system's boot configuration.
grub-sec-4: Environment Isolation: Uses targeted grep parsing instead of sourcing /mnt/etc/os-release to prevent host environment variable pollution during Chroot.
grub-sec-5: Bash Integrity: Resolved variable naming conflicts and unbound variable errors during automated Tier 1 execution for a flawlessly stable run.
grub-sb-1: Smart State Detection: Utilizes mokutil --sb-state to check if Secure Boot is enforced before attempting any GRUB installation.
grub-sb-2: Dynamic Shim Routing: Automatically forces the --uefi-secure-boot flag on Debian/Ubuntu systems to utilize Microsoft-signed shim binaries.
grub-sb-3: Arch Linux sbctl Integration: Detects custom Secure Boot keys and attempts to automatically sign the new GRUB binary using sbctl sign.
grub-sb-4: Automated MOK Enrollment: Imports the MOK.der key silently and feeds the generated One-Time Password to the system, leaving the user with clear instructions for their next reboot.
grub-luks-1: Early LUKS Detection: Scans for crypto_LUKS partitions before the Deep Scan Engine starts, preventing scan failures on encrypted drives.
grub-luks-2: Interactive Smart Decryption: Prompts to unlock partitions using cryptsetup to prevent lockouts.
grub-luks-3: LVM Auto-Activation: Automatically runs vgchange -ay to expose hidden Logical Volumes inside unlocked LUKS containers.
grub-luks-4: Auto-Cryptodisk Injection: Automatically appends GRUB_ENABLE_CRYPTODISK=y to /etc/default/grub ensuring the repaired system actually prompts for a password on boot.
grub-luks-5: Secure Relocking: Safely executes luksClose and deactivates volume groups after a successful repair to maintain data security.
grub-health-1: Smart Dependency Resolution: Automatically detects if crucial packages (grub, grub2, os-prober, efibootmgr, cryptsetup, mokutil) are missing inside the target broken system.
grub-health-2: Multi-Package Manager Support: Dynamically utilizes pacman, apt-get, dnf, or zypper to seamlessly install missing dependencies on the fly.
grub-health-3: DNS Tunneling (resolv.conf): Automatically copies the live host's /etc/resolv.conf into the chroot, ensuring the package managers have full internet access to download required fixes.
grub-univ-1: RedHat/Fedora Family Support: Full compatibility with Fedora, RHEL, CentOS, Rocky, and AlmaLinux.
grub-univ-2: Dynamic Command Routing: Automatically switches between standard grub-install / grub-mkconfig and the RedHat-specific grub2-install / grub2-mkconfig.
grub-univ-3: Smart Pathing: Intelligently manages configuration paths, dynamically creating and writing to /boot/grub2/grub.cfg or /boot/grub/grub.cfg as required by the host OS.
grub-intel-1: Kernel Cmdline Detection: Analyzes /proc/cmdline to instantly distinguish between Live ISOs (Archiso, Casper, etc.) and real installed systems.
grub-intel-2: Deep Scan Engine: Stealthily scans and mounts partitions in read-only mode to locate fstab and resolve UUIDs/PARTUUIDs before user interaction.
grub-intel-3: Unified One-Click Prompt: Combines environment detection and layout confirmation into a single, clean summary.
grub-intel-4: Automatic efivarfs Repair: Enhanced In-Situ logic to automatically mount efivarfs if the rescue environment fails to do so.
grub-v18: Added CLI Flags (--version, -env l/h, -auto) for complete Zero-Interaction Automation.
grub-v19: Added universal support for RedHat/Fedora/CentOS family (dynamic grub2 commands & paths).
grub-v20: Chroot Health Check - Auto-detects and installs missing GRUB/EFI packages with DNS resolv support.
grub-v21: LUKS & LVM Encryption Support - Auto-detects, unlocks (visible password), and configures GRUB_ENABLE_CRYPTODISK.
grub-v22: Secure Boot & Shim Integration - Auto-detects Secure Boot, handles shim-signed, and MOK Enrollment.
grub-v23: Current: Security Hardening & Bug Fixes - Dynamic MOK OTP, hidden LUKS passwords, config backups, and environment isolation.
grub-req-1: OS Families: Arch Linux, Debian/Ubuntu, RedHat/Fedora, SUSE, and derivatives.
grub-req-5: Secure Boot: Fully supported (Requires Motherboard MOK Enrollment via OTP).
grub-warn-v24: ⚠️ Planned for V24: Researching TUI (Text User Interface) implementation for a completely visual, menu-driven repair experience.
